$comment: Every WHO DAK artefact this platform has NOT implemented, and why.
A wrong rule gets noticed. A table nobody looked at does not — it simply is not there, and
nothing in the system is shaped like its absence. So the traceability guard fails on any
published artefact that is neither implemented nor listed here, and populating this file is
the scoping exercise rather than a formality.
decision: DEFERRED (intend to build), REJECTED (decided against), OUT_OF_SCOPE (belongs to
another domain), COVERED_ELSEWHERE (already implemented under different content).
Two entries are deferred on SAFETY grounds rather than effort — ANC.DT.02 and PNC.A4.DT.2,
the adolescent psychosocial screens. They collect the most sensitive information the
platform holds about a minor, and TSHEPO's SPECIALLY_PROTECTED class is currently
decorative. Those two must not be scheduled by convenience.

exclusions.reason: The antenatal danger-sign screen is the first ANC content this pack will ship. It is deferred only until the pregnancy episode and gestational dating exist, because most of its rows are gestation-scoped and a rule that cannot resolve a gestational age would report unassessed forever. Note the adaptation already identified: WHO's row for a convulsing woman outputs 'clinician's discretion', which is a defensible global hedge and an unacceptable national rule.

HEADSS adolescent psychosocial screening. Deferred on safety grounds, not effort: it collects the most sensitive information the platform holds about a minor — sexuality, drug use, abuse, suicidality — and TSHEPO's SPECIALLY_PROTECTED sensitivity class is currently decorative. ResourceSensitivityClassifier cannot return it, it shares a visibility tier with ordinary clinical data, and no caregiver-visibility suppression exists. Collecting this into a record that only looks protected is worse than not collecting it.
exclusions.revisitCondition: SPECIALLY_PROTECTED produces a distinct visibility tier, caregiver context is a first-class PDP input, and both access and refusal are audited (W8).

Intimate-partner violence enquiry and first-line support. Deliberately held to the confidentiality wave rather than the ANC wave: an IPV disclosure recorded where a partner can read it, or that triggers an SMS to a shared household phone, is more dangerous than not asking. It needs the safe-contact preference record and the send-path gate that honours it.

exclusions.reason: Deworming and intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy. Zimbabwe's malaria transmission is focal, so the national adaptation is a geography-conditioned rule rather than WHO's population-wide one.

ANC programme indicators. Deferred to the surveillance wave for a specific reason: an indicator computed before the clinical data behind it exists would report a coverage figure derived from an empty register, and a number is believed in a way an empty screen is not. They are also the strongest argument for the indicator engine reporting its own exclusions — an ANC figure reading 100% because 90% of contacts were never assessed is a lie told with a number.
exclusions.revisitCondition: ANC contact records exist in volume; IndicatorEngine (W10).

exclusions.reason: The postnatal contact schedule. Carries a known upstream defect: the published due and overdue columns for contacts 1 and 2 have their bounds inverted and appear shifted by one column. Our schedule will state the corrected windows as an explicit NARROWED adaptation naming the defect, and the extraction keeps WHO's text verbatim so the difference is visible.

Newborn immunisation schedule. Already implemented: CKP ships clinical/zw-epi-schedule.json and EpiForecastEngine, deployed and live-proven, using the Zimbabwe EPI schedule rather than a generic one. Re-implementing it here would create a second schedule for the same doses.
exclusions.revisitCondition: Only if the Zimbabwe schedule and the WHO PNC schedule diverge in a way the national schedule does not already resolve.

exclusions.reason: Contextual data for self-monitored blood pressure — device, validation status, training. This is what makes a home reading interpretable; a reading from an unvalidated device is not the same measurement as one from a clinic.

Health actions on a self-monitored blood-pressure reading. Depends on a series reducer that turns a stream of home readings into derived facts, so no aggregation operator has to be added to the shared predicate evaluator.
Danger signs reported alongside a home blood-pressure reading. WHO publishes this under the same identifier as the health-actions table; we qualify it so both stay visible.
